result:
**PASS.** On the current publication path, a generation that fails on an authored page-load error leaves the published link mirrors exactly as they were, and the typed-parameter refresh contract holds. I found no verified bug in this resolution, and no production change is needed.

**What the current code does.** The compile error comes up while `prepare` loads packages (`loadApp`), before anything is published. During that load, the newly generated declarations and the mirror contents are given to the compiler in memory only (`generatedOutput.overlay`). `publish`, which writes the files and syncs the mirrors (`links.sync()`), only runs from `finishGeneration` after a successful run. So on failure nothing is written, which is why the original defect (49 changed mirror files) no longer reproduces.

**Commands run** (Kit 3.1.0 from the installed pin; output is in `ephemeral/validation-253/`):

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| Baseline: `go test ./internal/gen -run '^(TestFailedPageLoadGenerationPreservesPublishedMirrors\|TestTypedLoadParamsRefreshBeforeStaleHandlerCompilation)$' -count=1 -v` | both PASS (3.5s) |
| Mutation: sync the mirrors in `prepare` before `loadApp` (the original defect's shape) | new test FAILS at `output_test.go:91`: "generation temporarily changed published mirrors before authored code compiled" |
| Mutation: publish in `prepare`'s error path (the real failure path) | both FAIL: `output_test.go:102` (mirror bytes or membership changed) and `load_params_test.go:99` (failed generation changed `skgo_gen.go`) |
| Mutation: keep the refreshed params out of the in-memory compile view | typed-params test FAILS at `:91`: the error no longer names `Label`, so that assertion is what proves the refresh |
| Temporary edit: run the new test with a real cache directory (the CLI default is the cached path; `fixtureConfig` turns the cache off) | PASS, with three cache misses and no fallback to the uncached path, so the cached path is covered too |

One extra mutation, publishing when `p.Run()` fails, did not make either test fail. That was not a gap in the tests: the compile error happens earlier, in `Prepare`, so that code never ran. The mutation in `prepare`'s error path replaced it.

**Is the new test load-bearing?** Yes. It runs the real generator on the `typed-load-evolution` fixture plus remote, page-load and pending sources the test writes itself. It requires the exact authored error, compares all mirror paths and bytes against what the successful run produced, checks again while the failing run is still loading packages, then confirms recovery after the repair (the pending file gets published and `go build ./internal/skgo/...` succeeds).

**One thing for you to confirm (not a bug):** the issue says refreshed typed-param declarations "must remain refreshed" on disk after a failed generation. That rule was changed on purpose in #266 (`c6906b7b`), whose worklog says "blank-and-restore is not the contract." Now the refreshed params are used when compiling (the error names `Label`, which only exists if the refresh happened), but a failed run leaves the published params unchanged. They get written on the next successful run. The existing regression in `internal/gen/load_params_test.go` enforces this. If you still want the issue's literal on-disk wording, that would reverse #266; otherwise #253 can close.

**State:** every temporary mutation is restored; `git status` matches the start apart from the new `ephemeral/validation-253/` logs. I made no implementation changes and no commits. The implementer's `02-opus-review.json` and `.err` are empty files.
